sheet-80.description: Sheet 80 of volume 3 of the Sanborn Essex County series covers the southern and western part of Essex Fells Borough, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right of the page. The sheet is crossed by Roseland Avenue, which runs across the upper third of the page, and is bounded at the top right by the Caldwell Branch of the Erie Railroad and its passenger station, with a small garage next to it. Wootton Road curves from the station down to Roseland Avenue, where it continues south as Hathaway Lane; Oak Lane runs along the right side of the sheet, and Rensselaer Road loops from Roseland Avenue around the lower half of the page to meet Forest Road near the bottom right corner. A further street between Hathaway Lane and Oak Lane is drawn and marked as not opened. The area is a planned residential park in its early years: large lots with scattered frame dwellings, many marked as the property of Jas. W. Paul Jr. and numbered, a club house, a public school, a spring house and the greenhouses of Henry Rudolph, florist, on the north side of Roseland Avenue. Six- and four-inch water pipes and hydrants are drawn along most streets. Much of the sheet, especially the lower left and the large block between Rensselaer Road and Hathaway Lane, is open land with property lines only. Margins point to sheets 81 and 82 to the right; the other margins are marked 0 (not mapped).
notes: Forest Road is today's Forest Way.
The street drawn between Hathaway Lane and Oak Lane is marked (Not Opened); no modern street follows it.
The diagonal street crossing Rensselaer Road in the lower left (unnamed on the sheet) follows today's Welsh Road west of Rensselaer Road; its continuation east to Hathaway Lane no longer exists.
Caldwell Branch of Erie R.R. and passenger station at the top right; the line is abandoned today.
Scale 100 ft to one inch; the fitted scale agrees.

map, 100 ft. Southern Essex Fells: Roseland Av, Wootton Rd, Hathaway Lane, Oak Lane, Rensselaer Rd, Forest Rd (now Forest Way); Erie RR Caldwell Branch station top right. North to upper right (rotation about 53 deg). One part. Curved streets; one hand-picked junction.

sheet-81.description: Sheet 81 covers the northern part of Essex Fells Borough and its boundary with Caldwell Borough, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The Caldwell Branch of the Erie Railroad crosses the sheet from top to bottom just right of centre, and a creek, unnamed on the sheet, winds from the top centre to the lower left. The left third is the open land of Caldwell Borough and West Caldwell Borough, with Brookside Avenue running diagonally across it, a wind mill tower and a covered reservoir. East of the railroad the sheet is laid out in residential blocks: Wootton Road runs north from Oak Lane past Runnymede Road and Buttonwood Road to Manheim Road at the Caldwell line, and Roseland Avenue runs along the right edge with Hawthorne Road leaving it eastward. Buttonwood Road crosses the railroad and loops west of it to Runnymede Road, enclosing the Essex Fells Water Company's pumping station with its reservoir and wells. Runnymede Road runs from the far left across the railroad to Roseland Avenue, and Oak Lane crosses the bottom of the sheet near the passenger station. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings on large lots, several belonging to the estate of F. F. Thompson and to J. P. and G. P. Scholfield, with L. J. Francisco's livery at Manheim Road, Wm. Whitcher's livery with the borough hose cart, and St. Peter's Episcopal Church near the junction of Runnymede Road and Roseland Avenue. Margins point to sheets 85 (top), 80 (bottom) and 82 (right).
notes: Hawthorne (Road), lettered at the right edge where it leaves Roseland Avenue, is today's Forest Way at that end.
The Buttonwood Road segment drawn crossing the railroad to Wootton Road no longer exists; today's Buttonwood Road is the north-south part west of the railroad.
Oak Lane / Wootton Road is drawn as two offset junctions about 30 m apart; the single modern node fitted neither (26 m off) and was left out.
Caldwell Branch of Erie R.R. is abandoned today.
Header reads Essex Fells & Caldwell Borough, N.J.

map, 100 ft. Northern Essex Fells and Caldwell boundary: Wootton Rd, Runnymede Rd, Buttonwood Rd, Manheim Rd, Roseland Av, Oak Lane, Brookside Av; Erie RR Caldwell Branch; water company pumping station. North to upper left (about -36 deg). One part.

sheet-82.description: Sheet 82 covers the eastern part of Essex Fells Borough, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Roseland Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet from Manheim Road and the Caldwell Borough line at the top to Oak Lane at the bottom; the dash-dot borough line crosses the upper part of the sheet. Benjamin Lane runs east from Roseland Avenue to the E. A. Benjamin property. Hawthorne Road leaves Roseland Avenue, turns north past a junction with Forest Road and curves northeast to the top right corner, crossing the head of Hathaway Lane. Forest Road runs southeast to cross Hathaway Lane in the lower centre, Hillside Road crosses from Hathaway Lane to Rensselaer Road and beyond, and Rensselaer Road runs up the right side of the sheet. Runnymede Road appears at the left edge joining Roseland Avenue. A street parallel to Roseland Avenue in the lower left is marked as not opened. The district is a newly laid out residential park with large, mostly empty lots and a few substantial dwellings, several marked as the property of J. W. Paul Jr., with the houses of Geo. H. Beardsley, Walter Brown, Mrs. C. W. Leavitt, J. B. White and Geo. E. Weyl, a covered well and greenhouses. Six- and four-inch water pipes and hydrants run along the streets. Margins point to sheets 85 and 86 (top), 81 (left) and 80 (bottom); the right margin is marked 0.
notes: Hawthorne Road between Roseland Avenue and Forest Road, and Forest Road, are today's Forest Way; the northeast arm of Hawthorne Road keeps its name.
Hillside Road is today's Hillside Lane.
Benjamin Lane has no modern counterpart in the same position (today's Park Lane lies about 50 m south).
The hand-picked Hathaway Lane / Hillside Lane junction disagreed with the fit by about 5 m and was left out.

map, 100 ft. Eastern Essex Fells: Roseland Av, Hawthorne Rd and Forest Rd (now Forest Way / Hawthorne Rd), Hathaway Lane, Hillside Rd (now Hillside Lane), Rensselaer Rd, Benjamin Lane. North to upper left (about -36 deg). One part; one hand-picked junction.
